restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each is one padded block M || 0x86 with zero capacity (520 fixed state bits). Complete fixed-zero-IV SHA3-256 sponge with suffix 0x06 and pad10*1, prefix rounds 0..4, 256-bit digest.

No advice: the algorithm runs every phase itself - the trail search P (trail_search in the experiment file, whose T3 counter of full evaluations raises CapReached above F_CAP = 2^30), the advice program B', setup S, the connector and the enumeration E - and its time is the sum of caps and exact counts times counted prices (proof 2, 6): P 2^33.652 units (T1 8,674,833 nodes x 2^12; T2 1,639,088,128 leaves x 166; T3 5,679,328,446 batches x 1,583; full evaluations at F_CAP x 2^13; 1411 group setups x 2^27); B' 2^32 units plus one update, at most 2^26 units per candidate, with constants no run chose (no attempt limit per candidate, DMIN 33, unweighted order); at most 2^13 connector attempts of at most X_MAX = 2^23 work units; E: K = 96 spaces of 2^24 batches of 256 pairs at 6,112 primitives per batch on every path; at most S2CAP = 2^24 stage-2 pairs per space. Algorithm 2^35.0558.

Development (proof 0.0-0.1, H2): this package's algorithm, constants, caps and experiments are byte-identical to winglock v14 (f1cedf6, pending 37.05); tree 69546ed. v14's own development (G2, C) is inherited by lineage, not charged here: no run of ours since e3ce051 fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number the algorithm reads (our work was an exact-rationals audit of v14's ledger, local re-runs of the shipped experiments, and re-verification of the 16 certificates; all measure-only, below 2^28.5 units even at worst-reading caps). Total = the algorithm term alone: 2^35.0558, claimed 35.06, integer-power tight both ways (2^35.06 exceeds the exact sum, 2^35.05 does not); preprocessing (P + B' + S) 2^34.0509, claimed 34.06. Sensitivities (proof 0.0, 0.1): inheriting v14's charged development gives 36.18 (G2 only), 37.05 (G2 + C, v14's own total), or 37.45 (C's spaces with their stage-2 cap term).

Premise P (inside H1; success only): P outputs the trail of proof 3 within F_CAP, from two native runs over all 1.4 x 10^12 leaves (F = 770 in the algorithm's order; 1,896,302 in pass 1, which bounds the algorithm's F for any core order by proof Lemma P, 566 times below F_CAP = 2^30; Appendix A). The organizer executes the algorithm's own P on sub-problems (r5-count trials 24-27) and recounts T1-T3 (r5-trail-0..3). If F exceeded F_CAP, P would stop without output: every cost bound holds either way. E is v8's E as a function of the space (proof Lemma 4).

Probability space: the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), fixed target, no advice. Success is measured end to end (proof 5): each of the 48 runs of the R5 study is a complete run of v14's algorithm (proof Lemma 6), and 46 of 48 output a collision. Under premise R the outcomes are independent Bernoulli(p) draws; the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound is 0.874. Claimed 0.40, which the data would still support with as few as 26 successes in 48. No per-advice, per-candidate or dispersion premise is used.

Executed evidence (not the claimed cost): the R5 study (plan, driver, analysis and enumerator hashed at 2026-10-07T20:27:28Z before any run; 48 runs, all reported; plan, commit record and per-run ledger verbatim in proof Appendix D). r5.py holds every run's advice, accepting attempt, space index and connector status string; r5-R-0..9 re-derive 20 seed-picked successes per review from their labels (advice, accepting attempt and up to 23 earlier attempts against the logged statuses, E's window) and return the collisions; r5-bpfull runs one whole B' from its label, shows both B' caps acting and recomputes 46/48 and the bound; 15 R5 collisions are certificates. Every other run since v11 (C, D, C', local re-derivations) is listed in proof 4.1.

Th0rgal is a co-author: 7deb1595 (with Subflatus3 and rubenmarcus) gave the zero-advice framing used here (v8's E also used its early-abort row order; v10's bitsliced E evaluates all equations). Subflatus3 (04395e26, d2df1a56) and GordoAR (bc0f7b56) also cap T3's full evaluations at 2^30; v14's value comes from the rule of proof 2.6, and none of their code, data or text is used. Memory: largest phase about 224 MB (T3's triple tables in the counted program); declared 30.

The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement over published work; no improvement on the method of Guo et al. is claimed beyond the byte-aligned adaptation, B', the bitsliced counted E and T3 and the accounting.

heuristics.statement: Averaged over all of the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), the probability p that v14's algorithm outputs a collision satisfies p >= p0 = 0.874. Premise R (run selection and coins): the SHA-256/SHAKE-256 coins of labels fixed before the runs act as fresh coins, and the 48 runs of the R5 study are an unselected sample of the algorithm's runs, so that their success indicators are independent Bernoulli(p) draws. Premise P: P outputs the trail of proof Section 3 within F_CAP.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability. Each R5 run is a complete run of the algorithm with label-derived coins (proof Lemma 6: B''s budget, A_MAX, X_MAX and the stage-2 cap never acted; CCAP and A_ADV acted as specified; E ran on the accepted spaces in order to its first output), so its success indicator is the algorithm's. Premise P concerns success only: every cost term of P is an exact count or a cap. The claim 0.40 needs p >= 0.40; output correctness and every cost cap hold without H1.
heuristics.extrapolation: 46 of the 48 R5 runs succeed (first output at spaces 1-89); runs 6 and 31 had none in 96 spaces. Under premise R the 48 outcomes are independent Bernoulli(p) draws (distinct labels by themselves only give distinct SHAKE-256 streams), and p0 is the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound (exact binomial tail). 0.40 would still be the 95% bound with 26 successes in 48. Premise R: the plan, driver, analysis and enumerator were hashed before any run (20:27:28Z); every run is reported (proof 4.3, Appendix D); the plan's only outcome-dependent rule is whether to claim, which keeps the bound's coverage; every other run since v11 is listed (proof 4.1). Organizer checks: r5-R-0..9 re-derive 20 seed-picked successes per review from their labels, including their place among the accepted spaces; r5-bpfull re-runs one whole B' and recomputes the count; 15 collisions are certificates. Premise P: two native runs of T3 over all batches (pass 1 bounds the algorithm's F by Lemma P, 566 times below F_CAP), organizer recounts of T1-T3 and of P on sub-problems. Descriptive: 0.037 positive spaces per space against 0.0265 predicted by the trail; v13's tuned B' gave the same 46 of 48.
heuristics.limitations: 48 complete runs. Label-seeded SHAKE-256 coins stand in for fresh words (premise R). The runs' E is fes.c (exact enumeration, self-checked at 64 points per space; Lemma 4 makes it the same function of the space as the counted E). Failures and the order of spaces are logged by us; the organizer re-derives 20 seed-picked successes per review and their place among the accepted spaces, not the failures. P's full-scale output rests on our native runs (Appendix A); the organizer recomputes its counts and runs it on sub-problems.

heuristics.statement: The charged development of THIS package contains every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number this package's algorithm reads. Every constant, cap and experiment is adopted from winglock v14's published tree 69546ed by lineage and analysis; no run of ours fixed or could have changed any of them, so the charged development is 0 and the total is the algorithm term alone. Runs that only measure a fixed algorithm (our audit and re-checks) fix no number: the same rule v14's H2 applies to its R5 study.
heuristics.scope: Only the development (preprocessing) part of the time and preprocessing claims. The algorithm's own terms (2^35.0558) are caps and exact counts at counted prices and do not depend on H2.
heuristics.extrapolation: Proof 0.1 lists every run with what it fixed and the claim it would give if charged: A1 41.04, A2 38.74, R5 37.88, C' 41.29, D 37.58, A3/A4 37.87, native P runs 37.42; all but A1 and C' together 39.51. Proof 0.2 gives the origin of every number in B', the connector, the driver and E: each is analysis, literature, the rule of proof 2.6, or a charged run (G2, C). B''s three tuned settings of v13 (A2) are replaced by values that no run chose and that two plans (C' at 16:58:33Z, R5 at 20:27:28Z) fixed before any of their runs; the R5 study measures the success with them (46 of 48, the same as v13's tuned B'), so no tuned number is load-bearing. B''s code reads only P's trail and the fixed bits.
heuristics.limitations: If the panel holds that v14's upstream sizing runs (G2, C) travel with the reused constants, this package's claim becomes 36.18 (G2 only), 37.05 (G2 + C at v14's prices, v14's own total), or 37.45 (C's spaces with their stage-2 cap term). All readings are disclosed in proof 0.0-0.1; the claim takes the zero-inheritance reading because every number this package reads traces to v14's published tree, not to a run of ours.
